title: Cedarwood and frankincense reed diffuser
subtitle: A warm woody diffuser for living rooms and studies
excerpt: A reed diffuser blend of cedarwood and frankincense essential oils in a dipropylene glycol base. Wicks steadily from a narrow-necked bottle through rattan reeds. Lasts three to four months in a 100 ml bottle.
sourceNotes: Reed diffuser base and wicking action: general aromatherapy and home fragrance formulation literature. Dipropylene glycol safety data: open-access MSDS sheets, SDS for dipropylene glycol (Sigma-Aldrich, freely available). Cedarwood and frankincense essential oil properties: IFRA guidelines and general reference.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~100 ml diffuser liquid (one 100 ml bottle; lasts 3 to 4 months)
recipe.batchNotes: Make a 200 ml batch to fill two bottles.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix the concentrate and store in a sealed dark bottle; fill the diffuser vessel as needed.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: In the diffuser bottle: three to four months as the liquid wicks away. Mixed but unused in a sealed dark bottle: six months. Discard if the liquid turns cloudy or develops a sharp rancid smell. Replace the rattan reeds when they stop wicking (usually after three months).

glossaryTerms.definition: Dipropylene glycol (DPG) is a synthetic, nearly odourless liquid used as a carrier in reed diffusers. It has a low viscosity that allows rattan reeds to wick it up by capillary action, and it releases the fragrance oils gradually as it evaporates at room temperature.

content.text: This is a cedarwood and frankincense reed diffuser blend for living rooms and studies. The

carries the essential oils up through the rattan reeds and releases them slowly into the room. The cedarwood note is warm and woody; the frankincense deepens it with a faint incense quality. A 100 ml bottle with seven or eight reeds will fragrance a medium-sized room for three to four months.

items.prepNote: the wicking carrier; 85% of the blend

content.text: Weigh the DPG into the diffuser bottle.
Add the cedarwood and frankincense essential oils. Swirl gently to blend.
Insert seven to eight rattan reeds. Flip all the reeds immediately to saturate both ends; from then on, flip two or three reeds once a week to refresh the scent throw.

Place the diffuser in a room with a gentle air current (near a door or vent) to aid evaporation. Keep away from direct sunlight and heat sources, which cause the liquid to evaporate too quickly. Do not place the bottle on polished wood surfaces; DPG can mark some lacquers. Stand on a coaster.

Three to four months in an active diffuser. Replace the reeds when they stop wicking; they saturate with dust and old oil after about three months. The mixed liquid, stored in a sealed dark bottle, keeps six months.
